findings.title: SceneRevision cannot express unverified/estimated time although SCENE_TIME_UNVERIFIED exists
findings.root_resolution: time_basis + verified carriers; missing/non-monotonic PTS fails the detect job; legacy unverified scenes cannot start analysis
evidence: candidate $defs/SceneRevisionInfo requires time_basis (decoded_pts|estimated|unverified) and embeds the canonical Scene (with verified)
invariant 'scene.verified iff time_basis==decoded_pts'
G13 a SceneRevisionInfo without time_basis is rejected by the candidate schema
S09 the DDL CHECK enforces (verified=1 AND time_basis='decoded_pts') OR (verified=0 AND time_basis!='decoded_pts')
S02 legacy scene rows are backfilled verified=0 / time_basis='unverified' with no invented verification
D02/D03 request error SCENE_TIME_UNVERIFIED=422 and terminal segment job status failed are both declared
findings.notes: Enforcement that only verified+decoded_pts may start analysis remains an application rule (declared in schema invariants and docs/31), as expected for a design candidate.

findings.title: candidate FrameRef has the same name but a different shape, so per-shot frames cannot be stored in canonical model_run.frames
findings.root_resolution: rename to ShotFrameRef with the full canonical shape including target_seconds/time_basis; real frames stored in model_run_artifacts
evidence: C04 no component-name collision with the canonical namespace (the 1.0 FrameRef collision is gone)
B03 ShotFrameRef is shape-compatible with canonical FrameRef (target_seconds/time_basis present, sha256 pattern identical, required set not larger)
B04 a generated ShotFrameRef instance validates against the canonical FrameRef
B05 the four real live-15 frame references validate as ShotFrameRef
S15 model_run_artifacts.frames_json exists; canonical ModelRun.frames is the read path
findings.notes: N4: ShotFrameRef keeps an anyOf[integer,null] branch for source_pts/time_base_num/time_base_den while also declaring a sibling type:integer, so the null branch can never validate (G15). The effective behaviour matches the stated intent (per-shot real PTS only) but the schema text is self-contradictory.

findings.title: no immutable child plan and no shot/boundary binding storage, so the fixed denominator cannot be guaranteed
findings.root_resolution: parent/item/seal created in one transaction; count/ordinal seal trigger; worker may only claim a sealed plan
evidence: S15 shot_batch_parent / shot_batch_item / shot_batch_seal / attempt_execution exist with the promised columns
S05 a parent with fewer items than planned_count cannot be sealed (INCOMPLETE_BATCH_PLAN)
S06 a plan with an ordinal gap (items 0 and 2 for planned_count=2) cannot be sealed
S07 a claim that joins the seal sees 0 children before the seal and 2 after it
S08 parent/item/seal rows are immutable after insert (update/delete/append all abort)
S16 the generic V2 batch_child table keeps its original two columns and stays empty
S14 job/attempt status rows stay mutable under their own CAS
findings.notes: The 'all jobs + parent + items + seal in one transaction' rule is an owner-side code rule stated in docs/31, not a DDL constraint - expected for a design candidate.

findings.title: AnalysisBinding has no lease/fencing token and scene_revision_hash has neither algorithm nor storage

findings.title: no terminal state for not-executed/deadline children and the parent deadline is not observable
findings.root_resolution: deadline -> failed + BATCH_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, user cancel -> cancelled + JOB_CANCELLED, model_started derived from attempt_execution, no Job enum extension
evidence: D01 ChildSummary.status and ParentJob.status are subsets of the canonical Job.status enum; no 'not_run' value exists (G06 rejects it)
D02 terminal error table maps BATCH_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED -> child failed / parent failed, JOB_CANCELLED -> child cancelled / parent cancelled, CHILD_ANALYSIS_INCOMPLETE -> parent partial
BatchChildrenResponse invariants state the deadline and cancel mapping and that all planned rows are retained
S11 model_started is derivable from a persisted attempt_execution.model_action_at, not from a claimed CPU task

findings.title: ShotEvidence cannot satisfy the four-domain contract (R06) nor compile into the four per-shot targets

findings.title: the 1800 s parent deadline cannot cover its own 12 children (12 x 420 s = 5040 s)
findings.root_resolution: parent budget = 450*n+90 (max 5490), per child 420 s + 30 s release
evidence: F01 450*n+90 for n=1..12 never exceeds 5490 and 450*12+90 = 5490; the old 1800 s constant is gone from plans/v1-revised-plan.json limits
F01 420 s analysis + 30 s release = the declared 450 s per-child budget
docs/31: the deadline is fixed at created_at, is public via ParentJob.deadline_at, is not extended on restart, and truncated children are kept as failed rows (never deleted)
D02 the truncation terminal code is declared (BATCH_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED)
findings.notes: The budget is now arithmetically able to cover the fixed denominator; whether a real machine meets it remains a pilot question (see M11) and the design forbids shrinking the denominator on overrun.

new_findings.title: the ETag response header is not machine-declared in the overlay, and the metadata_only promotion rule is undefined
new_findings.trigger: the implementer builds the effective-openapi from base + overlay and has to decide where the ETag header goes
new_findings.expected: an OpenAPI responses.200.headers entry (header name ETag, string schema, the quoted strong tag format) plus a written rule for how metadata_only is promoted into the effective document
new_findings.actual: the overlay has no 'headers' key anywhere (C08); the header exists only as free text in a bespoke map whose merge semantics are not defined, while the exact format is written down in docs/31 and the machine contract
new_findings.evidence: C08; docs/31 'strong ETag = quoted scene:<scene_revision_id>:<hash>'; plans/v1-multishot-contract.json scene_hash.etag
new_findings.note: Does not change any DTO shape; it leaves the ETag half of the M1 remedy in prose.

new_findings.title: the machine contract's additive_paths list omits the new GET /api/v1/scenes/{id} that the overlay adds
new_findings.where: plans/v1-multishot-contract.json additive_paths (6 entries) vs contracts/v1-multishot.openapi-overlay.json add_paths (7 entries)
new_findings.trigger: an implementer or a checker diffs the declared additive path set against the overlay
new_findings.expected: the declared set covers every path/method the overlay introduces, or new paths and new methods on existing paths are listed separately
new_findings.actual: the overlay adds a GET method on the existing path /api/v1/scenes/{id}; that path is absent from additive_paths, so a verifier using the contract list would not see the new GET

new_findings.title: the overlay marks only 2 of the 7 declared reuse paths as V1-usable
new_findings.where: contracts/v1-multishot.openapi-overlay.json metadata_only (2 keys) vs plans/v1-multishot-contract.json reuse_paths (7 keys)
new_findings.trigger: the M1 public surface is built from the reuse paths (scenes list, shots, shots/{id}, jobs/{id}, jobs/{id}/cancel) that docs/31 lists as M1 entry points
new_findings.expected: either a per-path/method V1-usable annotation for all M1 entry points, or an explicit rule that reuse paths need no promotion annotation
new_findings.actual: 5 条 reuse 路径在 overlay 中没有任何标注。canonical 中 /api/v1/scenes 的 GET 与 /api/v1/scenes/{id} 的 PUT 仍标 x-product-version: V2，overlay 只在 /api/v1/scenes/detect 标了 v1_profile、在 /api/v1/scenes/{id} 记了 ETag 说明；/api/v1/shots、/api/v1/shots/{id}、/api/v1/jobs/{id}、/api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel 本身已是 V1，却同样没有提升标注。

new_findings.title: ShotFrameRef keeps an unreachable anyOf null branch next to a sibling type:integer
new_findings.trigger: an implementer reads the anyOf and tries to accept a null source_pts, or a schema linter flags the contradictory keywords
new_findings.expected: either a plain non-null integer, or an anyOf without the contradictory sibling type
new_findings.actual: the null branch can never validate because the sibling type:integer applies at the same level (G15); the effective behaviour matches the stated intent (per-shot real PTS only) but the schema text says both things

new_findings.title: the bilingual evidence -> canonical Domains string[] mapping has no pinned language, ordering or entry rule
new_findings.where: contracts/v1-multishot.schema.json $defs/Character/SceneEvidence/Action (BilingualPhrase) vs canonical contracts/lvw.schema.json $defs/Domains (observation/inference/unknowns are string[])
new_findings.trigger: the per-shot adapter formats evidence into canonical Domains for the four-target compile
new_findings.expected: a pinned rule, e.g. one English entry per evidence item in Domains.observation/inference with the Chinese wording in text_zh, plus the ordering/dedup rule
new_findings.actual: docs/31 says only 'format each field by domain into canonical Domains.observation or inference' and 'the bilingual summary enters text_zh/text_en'; the canonical domain arrays have no language slot, so two implementations can legitimately diverge
new_findings.evidence: I08 (domains present) + canonical lvw.schema.json $defs/Domains (no language slot)

new_findings.title: the hashed field names time_base_num/time_base_den map onto the DDL columns tb_num/tb_den only inside the migration text
new_findings.where: plans/v1-multishot-contract.json scene_hash.fields vs contracts/v1-multishot-migration.sql lvw_scene_hash(s.media_ref_id, m.sha256, s.version, ..., s.tb_num, s.tb_den, ...)
new_findings.trigger: the shared hash function is implemented or ported outside the migration
new_findings.expected: the mapping between hashed field names and DDL column names is declared in the machine contract, not only implied by the SQL call site
new_findings.actual: the contract lists the hashed field names but not the column aliases; a port that hashed the column names would produce a different, silently incompatible hash
new_findings.evidence: D04 (SQL call argument order and names vs contract field list)
